extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners handling continuation/divisional/CPA filings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural guidance for filing and examining divisional, continuation, continuation-in-part (CIP), and Continued Prosecution Applications (CPA) under U.S. practice (MPEP §201.06). Covers entitlement to benefit, oath/declaration, specification/drawings, incorporation by reference, inventorship, examination, publication, and CPA-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Divisional Application
rubrics_metrics.description: A later application for an independent or distinct invention, carved out of a pending application and disclosing and claiming only subject matter disclosed in the earlier or parent application, is known as a divisional application or 'division.' The divisional application should set forth the portion of the earlier disclosure that is germane to the invention as claimed in the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often filed after a restriction requirement by the examiner. A divisional may depart from phraseology used in the parent but not in substance; any variation amounting to 'new matter' relative to the parent is impermissible. See related MPEP sections (§201.08, §201.11). Use form paragraph 2.01 to notify applicant of possible divisional status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Benefit/Claim Requirements for Divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: The divisional application must claim the benefit of the prior nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 121 or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §201.11 for conditions to receive the benefit of the filing date of the prior application. To claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c) include a specific reference per 37 CFR 1.78(a) in the first sentence(s) of the specification or in an application data sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper Filing Rule for Divisional Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional applications of utility or plant applications must be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Divisional applications of design applications may be filed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.53(b) or 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.60 and 1.62 were deleted; applicants should identify continuations/divisionals appropriately to avoid misprocessing. Applications filed under 1.53(b) are the 'default' application type and are processed as 35 U.S.C. 111(a) filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do Not Call a 119(e) Provisional-Benefit Application a 'Division'
rubrics_metrics.description: An application claiming the benefits of a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) should not be called a 'division' of the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent term calculations differ: provisional-benefit application has patent term from its own filing date, whereas applications under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) may have term calculated from the earliest application date if properly claimed. Cite 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2) and (a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Parent Application Classification and Status on Papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are requested to include the appropriate USPTO classification of the divisional application and the status and assigned art unit of the parent application on papers submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification appears in the Office communication where restriction was made; suggested placement: upper right corner of transmittal letter or in an application data sheet per 37 CFR 1.76(b)(3). This expedites processing and assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design Application as Division of Utility — Eligibility and Filing Route
rubrics_metrics.description: A design application may be considered a division of a utility application (but not of a provisional application) and is entitled to the filing date thereof if the drawings of the earlier utility application show the same article sufficiently to comply with 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a divisional design application may only be filed under the procedure set forth in 37 CFR 1.53(b), not under 37 CFR 1.53(d). See MPEP §1504.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on New Matter in Continuation/Divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date; continuation/divisional application specification and drawings must not contain subject matter that would have been 'new matter' in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new matter is present in a continuation/divisional filed with only a copy of prior oath/declaration, the examiner should notify applicant in the next Office action and require (A) a new oath/declaration with surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) and (B) redesignation as a continuation-in-part. Use form paragraph 2.10.01 to require correction of relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.53(b) Filing Date Completeness Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For a complete filing date under 37 CFR 1.53(b), an application must include a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 (description pursuant to 37 CFR 1.71), at least one claim pursuant to 37 CFR 1.75, and any drawing required by 37 CFR 1.81(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory filing fee and an oath/declaration are also required by 37 CFR 1.51(b) but may be filed after filing date upon payment of surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f). Continuation, divisional, and CIP may be filed under conditions specified in 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) and §1.78(a). See MPEP §201.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May File Under 1.53(b) vs. 1.53(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) A continuation or divisional naming the same or fewer inventors as the prior application may be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or (d). (2) A continuation-in-part or a continuation/divisional naming an inventor not named in the prior application must be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely watch inventor listings when choosing filing route; naming a new inventor compels newly executed oath/declaration under 1.53(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/Declaration Requirements — General (37 CFR 1.63(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath or declaration is not required in a continuation or divisional application provided: (i) the prior nonprovisional application contained an oath/declaration; (ii) the continuation/divisional is filed by all or fewer than all inventors named in the prior application; (iii) the specification and drawings contain no matter that would have been new matter in the prior application; and (iv) a copy of the executed oath/declaration from the prior application is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy must show the signature or an indication of signature (e.g., '/s/'). If naming an inventor not in prior application, a newly executed oath/declaration must be filed. If power of attorney or correspondence address changed, identify the change in the continuing/divisional or Office may not recognize it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion of Inventor Names When Using Prior Oath Copy
rubrics_metrics.description: The copy of the executed oath/declaration submitted must be accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of the name(s) of person(s) who are not inventors in the continuation/divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deletion statement must be signed by person(s) authorized under 37 CFR 1.33(b) to sign an amendment. If no deletion statement is provided, the continuation/divisional will be treated as naming the persons named in the copy of the oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching Copy of Prior Oath/Declaration to Correct Application
rubrics_metrics.description: When a copy of an oath/declaration from a prior application is filed, applicant should ensure the copy is matched with the correct application file (e.g., include a cover letter, adhesive label identifying application number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachments may be separated during initial processing; do not rely solely on a cover letter. Note 37 CFR 1.5(a) — no correspondence relating to an application should be filed prior to receipt of application number information from the PTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of Copies of Copies of Oaths/Declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the oath/declaration filed in the prior application is itself a copy of an earlier oath/declaration, either a copy of the copy or a direct copy of the original is acceptable (both are copies of the oath in the prior application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.4(d)(1)(ii) for authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates of Execution Not Required in Oath/Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent statute and rules do not require an oath/declaration to include a date of execution; no objection should be made because it lacks any date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant’s duty of candor and continuous duty of disclosure under 37 CFR 1.56 still applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and Drawings in Continuing/Divisional Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional may be filed with (A) a new specification and drawings and a copy of the signed oath/declaration from the prior application provided the new specification/drawings do not contain new matter; or (B) new specification/drawings and a newly executed oath/declaration provided no new matter is added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c), include a reference per 37 CFR 1.78(a) in first sentence(s) or application data sheet. Applicants should file a new set of claims as the original claims of the continuing application rather than relying on a preliminary amendment to avoid publication issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Amendments and Publication Risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) with a preliminary amendment that makes desired changes is NOT recommended because the changes may generally not be reflected in the patent application publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure the published application contains the desired claims, file the continuation/divisional with a new specification containing only the desired set of claims or submit the specification with amended claims through EFS.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Copy-of-Prior-Oath Cases Require Redesignation to CIP
rubrics_metrics.description: If a continuation/divisional filed with a copy of the prior oath contains subject matter that would have been new matter in the prior application, the examiner should notify applicant and require a new oath/declaration and redesignation as a continuation-in-part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should notify preferably in the first Office action. See MPEP §608.04(b) regarding new matter in preliminary amendments. Use surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) for newly executed oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by Reference of Prior Application (37 CFR 1.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may incorporate by reference the prior application by including an explicit statement in the continuation/divisional specification that the prior application(s) are 'hereby incorporated by reference.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after Sept 21, 2004, a claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78 is considered an incorporation by reference as to inadvertently omitted material subject to 37 CFR 1.57(a). Explicit incorporation by reference in the specification permits addition of subject matter from the prior application without petition, provided the continuation/divisional is entitled to a filing date. Incorporation added after the filing date is ineffective (no new matter after filing). Mere reference without explicit incorporation is not incorporation for 35 U.S.C. 112 disclosure purposes (In re de Seversky).

rubrics_metrics.name: When Application Is NOT Entitled to Filing Date — Petitions Required
rubrics_metrics.description: Material needed to accord an application a filing date may not be incorporated by reference unless an appropriate petition under 37 CFR 1.57(a)(3) or 37 CFR 1.182 is granted. Until petition granted, the application will not be entitled to a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after Sept 21, 2004, where needed material exists only in a prior-filed application, applicant may file petition under 37 CFR 1.57(a)(3) with fee under 37 CFR 1.17(f) and an amendment submitting the omitted material requesting that amendment be entered and filing date accorded as of original deposit date. See MPEP §201.17.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Omitted Material May Be Added After Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a continuation/divisional as originally filed (on/after Sept 21, 2004) is entitled to a filing date despite inadvertent omission of portion(s) of prior application(s), applicant may add omitted material by amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(a) within any time period set by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application included a proper explicit incorporation by reference statement, omitted pages/figures may be added by amendment provided omitted items contain only subject matter in common with properly incorporated document. If Office identified omitted items in a 'Notice of Omitted Item(s)', applicant need not respond to that notice but should submit amendment adding omitted material prior to first Office action to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship Carryover and Corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of a continuation/divisional by all or by fewer than all inventors named in a prior application without a newly executed oath/declaration is permitted. Applicant may (A) file a new oath/declaration signed by inventors for the continuing application or (B) file a copy of the prior oath accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of names not inventors in the continuation/divisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If continuation/divisional and copy of prior oath are filed without a deletion statement, the application will be treated as naming the inventors in the copy. A newly signed oath/declaration is required where an inventor not named in the prior signed oath is to be named. Deletion statements must be signed by person(s) authorized under 37 CFR 1.33(b). See MPEP §201.03 and §605.04(g) for file handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 47 (37 CFR 1.47) Issues for Non-Signing Inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the executed oath/declaration copy submitted was originally filed in a prior application accorded 37 CFR 1.47 status, the copy must be accompanied by a copy of the decision granting petition to accord 1.47 status unless all nonsigning inventors or legal representatives have filed an oath/declaration to join in an application of which the continuation/divisional claims benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one or more nonsigning inventors subsequently join, copies of their signed oaths must be submitted. New continuation/divisional applications filed under 1.53(b) with an unsigned oath copy and decision granting 1.47 status should be forwarded by OIPE to Office of Petitions; Office of Petitions will mail applicant a letter stating 'Rule 47' status has been accorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Attorney or Correspondence Address Must Be Identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Where power of attorney or correspondence address was changed during prosecution of the prior application, the change must be identified in the continuation/divisional application. Otherwise, Office may not recognize the change in the continuing/divisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.63(d)(4) requires identification of the change. Ensure records updated and clearly stated in continuing/divisional papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Entity Status Assertion Required in Continuing/Divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: If small entity status has been established in a parent application and remains proper and desired in a continuation/divisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), a new assertion as to continued entitlement to small entity status under 37 CFR 1.27 is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §509.03 for small entity practice and required statements/fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of Affidavits/Declarations from Prior Prosecution Do Not Automatically Carry Over (1.53(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131, 1.132) filed during prosecution of the prior nonprovisional application do not automatically become part of a continuation/divisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant desires to rely on earlier affidavits/declarations, make remarks of record in the 1.53(b) application and include a copy of the original affidavit/declaration filed in the prior application. Use form paragraph 2.03 to instruct applicant regarding affidavits/declarations in prior application. (Note: differences for 1.53(d) CPAs where affidavits may automatically carry over.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of Time to Establish Continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: If an extension of time is necessary to establish continuity between the prior and continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), the petition for extension of time must be filed as a separate paper directed to the prior nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3), an authorization to charge fees will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time in any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition. A continuing application is a new application with its own number and filing date and is not a 'reply' to the prior application's last Office action. Petitions must include certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 or 1.10 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Nonprovisional Is Not Automatically Abandoned on Filing Continuing Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.53(b) and 37 CFR 1.63(d) practice, the prior nonprovisional application is not automatically abandoned upon filing of the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To expressly abandon the prior application, a signed paper in accordance with 37 CFR 1.138 is required. If the prior application has a notice of allowance, prior can become abandoned by nonpayment of issue fee; if issue fee already paid, a petition to withdraw from issue must be filed before abandonment. If the prior is before the Board, appellant should notify Board of abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Practice for Continuation/Divisional Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: First action final practice applies to continuations and divisionals filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Any preliminary amendment present on the filing date is part of the original disclosure; amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., include a complete claim listing when a claim is added, canceled or amended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should be classified and assigned considering the claims that will be before the examiner upon entry of a preliminary amendment. If examiner finds new matter relative to prior application when a copy of prior oath was filed, notify applicant and require new oath and redesignation as CIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations on Preparing Continuing/Divisional to Control Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: To have an application publication of a continuation/divisional contain only the desired set of claims, it is strongly recommended the continuation/divisional be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) with a new specification containing only the desired set of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed with a copy of prior specification plus a preliminary amendment cancelling/amending/adding claims, publication may exclude the preliminary amendment unless the amended specification was also submitted through the Office’s Electronic Filing System (EFS). File preliminary amendments and IDSs early (preferably at filing) to avoid delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) — General and Form Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CPA practice under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (applicable primarily to design applications) was preserved for certain situations; CPAs have separate filing/processing requirements and specific forms (e.g., PTO/SB/29, PTO/SB/29A) and various defect notices (PTO-2011, PTO-2012, PTO-2018, PTO-2019, PTO-2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPAs are a special continued prosecution vehicle for design applications; if CPA requests are defective (e.g., not on separate paper), examiner should notify using form paragraph 2.31 for design CPAs. See forms list in MPEP §201.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA Inventorship and Inventive Entity Carryover
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventive entity set forth in the prior nonprovisional application automatically carries over into the CPA UNLESS the CPA request is accompanied by or includes on filing a statement requesting deletion of name(s) of person(s) who are not inventors of the invention being claimed in the CPA (37 CFR 1.53(d)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deletion statements must be signed by person(s) authorized under 37 CFR 1.33(b). If deletion is filed, examiner should acknowledge receipt using form paragraph 2.32. If CPA papers include a transmittal letter/new oath naming an inventor not in prior application and no 1.48 request filed, claims may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(f). Use form paragraph 2.33 to notify when a new inventor is identified without proper 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA — Benefit of Earlier Filing Date and Specific Reference Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a CPA is a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120 to every application assigned the application number identified in the request. Where an application claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 of a chain of applications, the application must reference the first (earliest) application and every intermediate application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.78(a)(2) explains that identification by application number is the specific reference required. In a chain of CPAs, references by application number constitute references to every CPA in the chain and the original non-continued prosecution application. For applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) seeking benefit of a CPA under 35 U.S.C. 120/121, a reference to the CPA by application number must appear in the first sentence(s) of the specification unless made in an application data sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA — Terminal Disclaimer Carryover
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed in the parent application carries over to a CPA (because the CPA retains the same application number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not want the terminal disclaimer to carry over, file petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with the required fee requesting that the terminal disclaimer filed in the parent application not be carried over. See MPEP §1490 for withdrawing a terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA — Prior Election Carryover Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An election made in the prior application carries over to the CPA only if all of the following conditions are met: (A) the CPA is designated as a continuation or not designated (i.e., NOT designated as a divisional); (B) there was an express election by applicant in reply to a restriction requirement in the prior application; (C) the CPA presents claim(s) drawn only to invention(s) claimed in the prior application; and (D) the CPA does not contain an indication that a shift in election is desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where conditions are met, examiner’s first action should repeat the prior restriction requirement to the extent still applicable in the CPA and state that prosecution is being continued on the invention elected and prosecuted in the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA — Information Disclosure Statements and Preliminary Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: All IDSs filed in the prior application that comply with 37 CFR 1.98 will be considered in a CPA by the examiner. IDSs filed before mailing of first Office action on the merits will be considered regardless of prior prosecution events. Applicants are encouraged to file IDSs and preliminary amendments at time of filing CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of IDS after first Office action could delay prosecution. Preliminary amendments filed after filing date may be denied entry under 37 CFR 1.115 if they unduly interfere with preparation of first Office action. If more time is needed, request a three-month suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(b) at the time of CPA filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA — Affidavits/Declarations Automatically Become Part of CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits and declarations (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131, 1.132) filed during prosecution of the parent nonprovisional application automatically become a part of the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, no copy of the original affidavit/declaration need be filed in the CPA. (Contrast with 1.53(b) practice where copies do not automatically carry over.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access to CPAs — Waiver of Confidentiality and Certified Copies
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA is construed to include a waiver of confidentiality by the applicant under 35 U.S.C. 122 to the extent that members of the public entitled under 37 CFR 1.14 to obtain access/copies/info concerning either the prior application or any continuing application may be given similar access to the other application(s) in the file. A certified copy of a CPA may be prepared upon request by the Certification Branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applications in the file jacket of a pending CPA are treated as pending (not abandoned) when determining access to copies and access. Certified copy will consist of the most recent non-continued prosecution application in the chain of CPAs and will show the CPA filing date as the filing date of that most recent non-continued prosecution application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and Notices Specific to CPA/Division Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific forms exist for CPA filing and for notices of defective CPAs or missing parts (e.g., Form PTO/SB/29, PTO/SB/29A, PTO-2011, PTO-2012, PTO-2018, PTO-2019, PTO-2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and applicants should use the indicated forms for transmittal, receipts, and notices. Use specific form paragraphs (e.g., 2.31–2.34) to communicate common defects or informational items to applicants.
